advances: An explicit rational padding in \(16(n+1)+1\) additional integer coordinates preserves the maximum atom, maximum reflected minimum mass, and curvature cutoff score exactly, forces Hellinger gain at least one eighth of the new integer dimension, and changes maximum actual depth by at most a factor of two. Consequently, a weak-Oertel bound on this high-gain class implies the unrestricted bound with half its constant; a logarithmic cutoff bound on this class implies the unrestricted logarithmic bound with one eighth its constant. Padding the exact rational family of accepted fact 604889294a17d7df gives actual bodies with linear Hellinger gain, uniformly vanishing reflected curvature, and cutoff score one while normalized total mass diverges. Their centered fibers give large actual depth, and their dimension growth also prevents them from disproving the logarithmic cutoff bound. Neither restricted lower bound, and therefore neither the locked conjecture nor the logarithmic cutoff conjecture, is proved by this reduction.

The scalar uniform bound and actual-depth comparison input are those of 03f071403cdfc69f; actual-table admissibility and the Hellinger normalization are those of ab57fac07c0d3160; the exact rebuilt rational tree family and its established estimates are those of 604889294a17d7df; the centered-fiber conclusion uses bb2b5f9519ae23e8. All padding geometry, zero-preserving extensions, center and cutoff calculations, product identities, parameter estimates, and the two reductions are proved above. statement:
Let \(n\ge1\). Use the admissibility hypothesis of accepted fact ab57fac07c0d3160: \(w=(w_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\) is a nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported table of finite real numbers, and there is a finite-valued function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) with \(f(z)=w_z\) at every integer point, including every zero, such that \(f((1-s)x+sy)\ge f(x)^{1-s}f(y)^s\) for \(0<s<1\). A zero endpoint makes the right side zero. Write \(A=\{z:w_z>0\}\), \(W=\sum_z w_z\), and \(M(w)=\max_z w_z\). Retain the canonical oriented displacement convention, including zero exactly once, and define

\[
\begin{aligned}
S_j(w)&=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^n}\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\},
&S_*(w)&=\max_{j\in\mathbb Z^n}S_j(w),\\
H_j(w)&=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^n}\sqrt{w_{j+v}w_{j-v}},
&H_*(w)&=\max_{j\in\mathbb Z^n}H_j(w),\\
G(w)&=\log\frac{2^nH_*(w)}W.
\end{aligned}
\]

For \(j\in A\), let \(\alpha_j(v)=\min\{w_{j+v},w_{j-v}\}\), \(\mathcal U_j=\{v:\alpha_j(v)>0\}\), and \(\Delta_j(v)=\log(w_j^2/(w_{j+v}w_{j-v}))\) for \(v\in\mathcal U_j\). In exactly the normalization of accepted fact 03f071403cdfc69f, put

\[
\begin{aligned}
B_j^\Delta(L)&=\sum_{\substack{v\in\mathcal U_j\\\Delta_j(v)\le L}}\alpha_j(v)
&& (L\ge0),\\
K_j(w)&=\max_{L\ge0}\frac{B_j^\Delta(L)}{1+L},
&K(w)&=\max_{j\in A}K_j(w),\\
\Delta_{\max}(w)&=\max_{\substack{j\in A\\v\in\mathcal U_j}}\Delta_j(v).
\end{aligned}
\]

All logarithms are natural. The maxima are attained. The Hellinger quantities and \(G\) agree with accepted fact ab57fac07c0d3160; \(S_*\) is the maximum of the \(S_{\mathbf J}\) used in accepted fact 604889294a17d7df after matching integer dimensions and center indices.

Set \(r=16(n+1)\), \(D=r^3\), and \(n'=n+r+1=17(n+1)\). For padding integer coordinates \(\xi=(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^r\) and continuous coordinates \(Y\in\mathbb R^D\), define

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_r&=\left\{(t,x):-1\le t\le1,\quad
 \frac{t-1}{2}\le x_i\le\frac{t+1}{2}\ (1\le i\le r)\right\},\\
a_r(t)&=1-\frac{1-t}{2r^2},\\
B_r&=\left\{(t,x,Y):(t,x)\in P_r,\quad
 |Y_\ell|\le\frac{a_r(t)}2\ (1\le\ell\le D)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then \(B_r\) is a full-dimensional rational compact convex polytope with integer dimension \(r+1\) and continuous dimension \(D\). Its nonempty integer fibers all have positive volume. Its exact integer support and weights \(u_\xi=\operatorname{vol}_D((B_r)_\xi)\) are

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_u&=\{(1,b):b\in\{0,1\}^r\}
 \;\cup\;\{(0,0)\}
 \;\cup\;\{(-1,-b):b\in\{0,1\}^r\},\\
u_{(1,b)}&=1,
&u_{(0,0)}&=\eta_r:=\left(1-\frac1{2r^2}\right)^{r^3},
&u_{(-1,-b)}&=\epsilon_r:=\left(1-\frac1{r^2}\right)^{r^3}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Every other integer weight is zero. Define \(F_r(\xi)=a_r(t)^D\) on \(P_r\), and \(F_r(\xi)=0\) outside \(P_r\). This is a finite-valued global log-concave extension of all of \(u\), including its zeros. The product table \(w'_{(z,\xi)}=w_zu_\xi\) is admissible with extension \(f'(z,\xi)=f(z)F_r(\xi)\). With \(Z_r=2^r(1+\epsilon_r)+\eta_r\) and \(\theta_r=Z_r/2^{r+1}\), it satisfies

\[
\begin{aligned}
M(w')&=M(w),&S_*(w')&=S_*(w),&K(w')&=K(w),\\
G(w')&\ge\frac{n'}8,
&\Delta_{\max}(w')&\le\Delta_{\max}(w)+\frac1{3r},\\
\frac{W'}{2^{n'}}&=\theta_r\frac W{2^n},
&\frac12\le\theta_r&\le\frac34,
&W'&=WZ_r,\\
\frac{|\operatorname{supp}w'|}{2^{n'}}
&=\left(1+\frac1{2^{r+1}}\right)\frac{|A|}{2^n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]

For the actual-body assertion, let \(n,d\ge1\), let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and assume \(S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\ne\varnothing\). Use the locked definitions \(C_z=\{y:(z,y)\in C\}\), \(w_z=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)\), \(W=\mathcal H_d(S)\), and \(h_S(p)=\inf_{H\ni p}\mathcal H_d(S\cap H)\), where \(H\) is a closed ambient halfspace. Empty and lower-dimensional fibers have weight zero. Let \(h_{\max}(C)=\max_{p\in S}h_S(p)\). Regroup the coordinates of \(C\times B_r\) so that its integer coordinates are \((z,t,x)\) and its continuous coordinates are \((y,Y)\), and call the resulting body \(C'\). It has integer dimension \(n'\), continuous dimension \(d+D\), and exact actual table \(w'\). For every such \(C\), including \(W=0\),

\[
\frac12h_{\max}(C)\le h_{\max}(C')\le h_{\max}(C).
\tag{2}
\]

When \(W>0\), the original actual table is admissible by accepted fact ab57fac07c0d3160, and (1) applies with its exact weights. In particular, for any fixed \(c>0\), a bound \(h_{\max}(C)\ge c\,2^{-n}W\) for all positive-mass actual bodies satisfying \(G(w)\ge n/8\) implies the same bound for all actual bodies with constant \(c/2\). A choice \(c\in(0,1/e)\) on the restricted class proves the locked statement with \(c_0=c/2\). Conversely any unrestricted bound restricts with no loss. Likewise, a bound \(K(w)\ge c\,W/[2^n\log(n+2)]\) for all admissible tables satisfying \(G(w)\ge n/8\) implies the unrestricted logarithmic bound with constant \(c/8\), and restriction in the other direction loses nothing.

The following family uses precisely the rational specialization of accepted fact 604889294a17d7df. For each integer \(k\ge8\), first set \(d_k=k^3\) and \(\rho_t^{(k)}=(1-t/k^3)^{k^3}\) for \(0\le t\le k\). Rebuild every tree parameter from these weights:

\[
\begin{aligned}
b_\ell^{(k)}&=0 &&(1\le\ell<8),
&b_\ell^{(k)}&=\left\lfloor\frac1{8\ell\rho_\ell^{(k)}}\right\rfloor
&&(8\le\ell\le k),\\
Q_{k,0}&=0,
&Q_{k,\ell}&=\sum_{j=1}^\ell b_j^{(k)},
&Q_k&=Q_{k,k},\\
m_k&=2(Q_k+1)^4,
&n_k&=1+\sum_{s=1}^{Q_k}m_k^s,
&\tau_k&=1-2^{-m_k}\binom{m_k}{m_k/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(a_0^{(k)}=0\), and \(a_s^{(k)}=\ell\) when \(Q_{k,\ell-1}<s\le Q_{k,\ell}\). Use the exact rooted-tree polytope \(P_{m_k,Q_k}\subset\mathbb R^{n_k-1}\) and coordinate tree \(\mathcal T_{m_k,Q_k}\) from the construction in that accepted fact, without changing its Boolean-chain successor or support. Its symbols \(n,N,\eta\) are respectively \(n_k-1,n_k,\tau_k\) here. Thus the exact rational body being selected is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat P_k
&=\left\{(x,t):x\in P_{m_k,Q_k},\quad 0\le t\le k,\quad
 t\ge a_{|u|}^{(k)}(x_u-1)\text{ for every }u\in\mathcal T_{m_k,Q_k}\right\},\\
C_k=C_{k,k^3}
&=\left\{(x,t,y):(x,t)\in\widehat P_k,\quad
 |y_i|\le\frac{1-t/k^3}{2}\ (1\le i\le k^3)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

In particular, no tree dimension or entrance count from the different log-affine profile is reused. Let \(w_k\) be this body's actual table, \(r_k=16(n_k+1)\), and let \(\widetilde C_k=C_k\times B_{r_k}\) with integer and continuous coordinates regrouped as above. Write \(\widetilde n_k=17(n_k+1)\), \(\widetilde d_k=k^3+r_k^3\), and \(\widetilde w_k\) for its actual table. To distinguish harmonic numbers from Hellinger sums, write \(H_k^{\mathrm{harm}}=\sum_{\ell=1}^k1/\ell\), which is the \(H_k\) in accepted fact 604889294a17d7df. These actual rational bodies satisfy

\[
\begin{aligned}
M(\widetilde w_k)=S_*(\widetilde w_k)=K(\widetilde w_k)&=1,
&G(\widetilde w_k)&\ge\frac{\widetilde n_k}8,\\
\Delta_{\max}(\widetilde w_k)
&\le\frac4{3k}+\frac1{48(n_k+1)}\longrightarrow0,\\
\frac{\widetilde W_k}{2^{\widetilde n_k}}
&=\frac{\theta_{r_k}}2\sum_{s=0}^{Q_k}\tau_k^s
      \sum_{t=a_s^{(k)}}^k\rho_t^{(k)},\\
\frac3{128}(H_k^{\mathrm{harm}}-H_7^{\mathrm{harm}})
&\le\frac{\widetilde W_k}{2^{\widetilde n_k}}
\le\frac34\left(1+\frac{H_k^{\mathrm{harm}}-H_7^{\mathrm{harm}}}{8}\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]

Consequently the ratio \(2^{\widetilde n_k}K(\widetilde w_k)/\widetilde W_k\) tends to zero even under the displayed high-gain and uniform curvature conditions. Nevertheless, each \(\widetilde C_k\) has one point, chosen before the halfspace, of actual depth at least \(2^{-\widetilde n_k-1}\widetilde W_k\), by the affine-selector theorem of accepted fact bb2b5f9519ae23e8. Moreover,

\[
0\le
\frac{\widetilde W_k}{2^{\widetilde n_k}\log(\widetilde n_k+2)}
\le
\frac{12k}{2^k\log2}
\left(1+\frac{H_k^{\mathrm{harm}}-H_7^{\mathrm{harm}}}{8}\right)
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{4}
\]

Thus this family disproves a constant-loss lower bound for \(K\) on the indicated class, but is neither an actual-depth counterexample nor a counterexample to the logarithmic \(K\) bound.
